top_paper.title: Behavioral Compositionality of Sparse Autoencoder Representations
top_paper.summary: Sparse autoencoder features are partially compositional but require interaction terms for accurate behavioral predictions and steering.

papers.title: Sparse Autoencoders Are a Shared Coordinate System for Symbolic Matching
papers.summary: SAE-IDF matches symbolic units across heterogeneous systems using sparse autoencoders and rarity-weighted features, enabling scalable neuro-symbolic reasoning.

papers.title: DuET: Note-Frame Dual Encoding for Piano Performance-to-Score Transcription
papers.summary: DuET is a dual-encoder transformer that jointly performs MIDI-to-score transcription and beat tracking to improve timing and duration accuracy in piano performance transcription.

papers.title: OpenMobile-2: Building Versatile Mobile Agents with Scalable Environments and App-Native Tools
papers.summary: OpenMobile-2 is an open mobile agent trained with diverse simulated apps, large-scale supervised and reinforcement learning data, and hybrid GUI-tool use, achieving strong benchmark results and real-device transfer.

papers.title: DuoDiscover: Scaling Autonomous Discovery Beyond the Evaluation Bottleneck
papers.summary: Evaluation has been central to advances in AI, and it is equally critical to autonomous discovery. Yet scaling autonomous discovery to real-world engineering challenges faces a fundamental bottleneck: the cost of evaluating progress. In real settings, a single true evaluation, such as a full benchmark or serving trace, can take hours, so a search can afford only a handful of true evaluations. We present DuoDiscover, a search system that jointly discovers what to optimize and how to evaluate progress efficiently, through three mechanisms. papers.title: From Research Goals to Scientific Closure: Evaluating Agents Through Evidence-Supported Physics Research
papers.summary: AI agents evaluated on physics research tasks show strong local scientific results but frequently fail to fully resolve research questions due to incomplete evidence and unresolved applicability limits.

papers.title: Speculative Sampling in Interactive Video Generation
papers.summary: Speculative Sampling enables interactive video generation with large bidirectional windows by caching predictions and delivering them incrementally, reducing latency without sacrificing quality.

papers.title: GeoState: Learning View-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling
papers.summary: GeoState introduces a view-independent geometric representation that separates scene dynamics from camera motion for predictive 3D world modeling, enabling consistent multi-view forecasting and cross-dataset generalization.

papers.title: Has GPT-6-Astra Achieved Embodied Intelligence?
papers.summary: GPT-6-Astra achieves high performance across diverse robotic tasks via in-context learning, yet real-world deployment reveals gaps in demonstration cost, execution time, and practical embodied intelligence.

papers.title: HexaShell: A Thin Harness for Exploring the Limits of VLM Agents as Robot Coding Agents
papers.summary: HexaShell is a coding agent that controls a dual-arm robot via vision and self-written tools, achieving state-of-the-art results on RoboDojo but struggling with contact-heavy tasks.

papers.title: OS-Helix: Unifying GUI Interaction and Code Execution in Native Computer-Using Agents
papers.summary: OS-Helix is an end-to-end trained multimodal agent that integrates GUI actions and code execution via hybrid supervised and reinforcement learning, achieving substantial gains on desktop automation benchmarks.

papers.title: DLite: History-free Speculative Decoding for Agentic AI
papers.summary: DLite improves speculative decoding for agentic AI by eliminating historical context maintenance and using target hidden states for local predictions, boosting acceptance length and reducing overhead.

papers.title: StopWatch: Goal Grounding for Object-goal Navigation
papers.summary: Explicit goal grounding fixes the dominant failure in vision-language navigation policies, yielding near-expert success with minimal policy changes.

papers.title: Persistent Planar Memory for Video World Models
papers.summary: PPMem is a video world model that uses compact plane primitives as persistent 3D memory to generate long coherent videos with explicit metric geometry.

papers.title: BizBench: Unveiling Hidden Challenges in Deploying Long-Horizon Agents for Real-World Business
papers.summary: BizBench evaluates long-horizon business agents on intermediate execution validity using real-world payment procedures, revealing that frontier models frequently violate constraints despite achieving partial goal success.

papers.title: Game2Real-Bench: Do Toy Games Reveal and Transfer to Real-World Visual Reasoning?
papers.summary: Visual reasoning is an important capability for vision-language models (VLMs) to understand visual evidence, spatial structure, constraints, and state changes. Existing evaluations mainly rely on real-world data or procedurally generated tasks. Real-world data preserve natural complexity, while procedural games provide controllable generation and verifiable solutions. However, it remains unclear whether abilities measured in toy games correspond to real-world visual reasoning and whether game examples can support transfer. papers.title: Into the Unknown: Benchmarking AI agents on open scientific research problems
papers.summary: Researchers benchmarked AI agents on open scientific problems by having them draft follow-up papers from unpublished directions, finding that none met expert standards and most contained fabricated claims or contradictory evidence.

papers.title: Tree-Aware Posterior Distillation for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: TreeOPSD enables long-horizon reinforcement learning for language model agents without critics by using tree-structured self-distillation with bounded updates derived from terminal rewards.

papers.title: DiscoveryRSI: Recursively Learning to Discover Valuable Hypotheses
papers.summary: DiscoveryRSI uses multi-agent evolutionary search and recursive learning to generate testable scientific hypotheses, improving quality through self-improvement and outperforming baseline agents on life-science benchmarks.

papers.title: Pack Light, CarryOn: Building Object-Oriented Context for Long-Horizon Agents
papers.summary: CarryOn organizes long-horizon agent context around reusable task objects rather than interaction histories, improving efficiency and performance on complex benchmarks.

papers.title: PRISM: PRIvileged Sibling-guided Multi-Agent Topology Design
papers.summary: PRISM improves multi-agent topology generators by recovering per-query preferences via privileged sibling-graph information, reducing cross-task drift.

papers.title: Mine, Sample, Render: Test-Time Diversity Alignment Of Generative Models
papers.summary: MSR improves generative diversity by mining categorical schemas from real artifacts to guide conditional rendering at test time.

papers.title: Behavioral Compositionality of Sparse Autoencoder Representations
papers.summary: Sparse autoencoder features are partially compositional but require interaction terms for accurate behavioral predictions and steering.

papers.title: Diminishing Returns of Data in Sparse Autoencoders: Functional Behavior does not Guarantee Feature Reproducibility
papers.summary: Sparse autoencoders can be trained with far fewer activation tokens when data budgets align with evaluation goals, though feature-level reproducibility demands larger scales.

papers.title: LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents
papers.summary: LEASH is a training-free framework that uses latent uncertainty to escalate from a weak to a strong computer-use agent only when needed and monitors the strong agent afterward, reducing cost while maintaining high success.

papers.title: Scalable Weak-to-Strong Verifier Hardening for Agent Environments
papers.summary: The study proposes an automated weak-to-strong loop that hardens agent environment verifiers against reward hacking by iteratively finding and repairing vulnerabilities in isolated sandboxes.

papers.title: LeanPRM: Lean-Grounded Process Supervision for Natural Language Proof Verification
papers.summary: LeanPRM uses the Lean proof assistant to automatically generate step-level correctness labels for natural-language mathematical proofs, enabling scalable training of learned verifiers without human annotation.

papers.title: Equal CER, Unequal Damage: Severity-Weighted Character Error Rate for OCR
papers.summary: A new metric called semCER uses an LLM judge to weight grapheme edits by severity, improving alignment with human ratings over standard character error rate for OCR and vision-language models.

papers.title: PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting of Multivariate Trajectories
papers.summary: PathFM is a trajectory-based forecasting model using flow matching to generate complete future paths, enabling efficient multi-path sampling and improved dependence modeling for time series.

papers.title: Learning to Read Out: Unembedding Dynamics in Language Model Pretraining
papers.summary: Hidden states encode task information before the readout expresses it, so behavioral timelines reflect readout learning rather than model acquisition, and faster readout training closes this gap earlier.

papers.title: Copy-Paste Language Models
papers.summary: Copy-Paste Language Models enhance in-context copying by adding a lightweight head that improves training efficiency, downstream performance, and long-context retrieval with minimal overhead.
